source.title: Dissecting components of reward: 'liking', 'wanting', and learning

confidence_rationale: This is the canonical statement of the exact decomposition MECH-055 asserts: reward is not one scalar but three dissociable psychological components -- 'liking' (hedonic impact), 'wanting' (incentive salience), and learning (predictive/PE associations) -- each with a partially distinct neural substrate. Crucially for MECH-055's NON-DEGENERACY PRECONDITION, the dissociations in this literature are established by INDEPENDENT PERTURBATION rather than by correlation: opioid microinjection into the accumbens hedonic hotspot raises 'liking' without a matched 'wanting' change, and mesolimbic dopamine manipulations raise 'wanting' without changing 'liking'. That is precisely the experimental form MECH-055's CONFIRMING clause demands. Source quality is high for a review (the underlying dissociations are among the most replicated findings in affective neuroscience) but this is a review, not a primary measurement, so it is capped below the 0.85 a well-powered primary study would earn. Mapping fidelity is good for axes 2 and 3 and their separation, but the paper is silent on REE's axis 1 (mu/kappa hedonic-stability), which the claim itself notes is NOT standard hedonic tone -- so the paper supports two of the three pairwise separations and cannot speak to the third. Held at 0.78 because the paper's own framing ('these components typically work together') is a live caveat against REE reading separability-under-intervention as non-degenerate variance under ordinary operation.
failure_signatures: Berridge et al. state the three components normally operate together and dissociate only under targeted intervention. A MECH-055 test that looks for non-degenerate variance during ORDINARY REE operation, with no manipulation designed to decouple the axes, could therefore report collapse even in an architecture that is genuinely separable -- making a null result uninformative rather than falsifying.

The biological asymmetry is severe and REE does not mirror it: 'liking' is generated by a small set of anatomically tiny, fragile hedonic hotspots (cubic-millimetre scale in rodent accumbens shell and ventral pallidum), while 'wanting' is distributed across the whole mesolimbic system. REE gives VALENCE_LIKING and VALENCE_WANTING equal-footing adjacent slots in one 6-dimensional vector, which is not the architecture this literature describes.

The 'learning' component in this decomposition is associative/prediction-error in general; it is NOT decomposed into a harm side and a benefit side. So this paper gives no support at all to the harm/benefit duality MECH-055 requires inside axis 3, which is the very half MECH-054's 2026-08-08 finding records as architecturally absent in REE.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reward is not a unitary process. It decomposes into at least three dissociable psychological components with partly separate neural substrates: 'liking' (the hedonic impact of a reward, measurable by orofacial affective reactions, mediated by opioid/endocannabinoid hedonic hotspots in nucleus accumbens shell and ventral pallidum), 'wanting' (incentive salience, the motivational pull toward a reward or its cues, mediated by mesolimbic dopamine and dissociable from hedonic impact), and learning (predictive associations and cognitive expectancies, including prediction-error-driven association formation). These components normally co-occur but can be pulled apart by targeted pharmacological and lesion manipulations, and their dissociation underlies disorders of mood and motivation including addiction, depression and eating disorders.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-055 asserts that hedonic tone, valence, and signed prediction error remain distinct channels rather than collapsing into one affect scalar. Berridge et al. supply the strongest available biological precedent for the non-collapse of exactly the pair REE calls axis 2 versus axis 3: hedonic impact ('liking' -> REE VALENCE_LIKING, index 1 in ree_core/residue/field.py) and incentive salience ('wanting' -> VALENCE_WANTING, index 0) are each separable from prediction-error-driven learning, and separable from each other. The claim's NON-DEGENERACY PRECONDITION (b) requires the VALENCE vector's components to be 'independently computable and independently perturbable'; this literature's method IS independent perturbation (intra-accumbens opioid agonist raises 'liking' without 'wanting'; dopamine sensitisation raises 'wanting' without 'liking'), which both validates the precondition as a biologically meaningful demand and tells REE what shape its own manipulation must take -- an intervention on one component's generator, not a passive correlation over a free-running rollout.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries, one of them serious. (1) The paper is silent on REE's axis 1. REE's 'hedonic tone' is mu/kappa, a softmax-temperature and commitment-threshold regulator -- a control-plane stability term -- and the claim's own NAMING NOTE concedes this is not the affective-neuroscience hedonic-tone construct. Berridge's 'liking' is REE's axis 2, not REE's axis 1. So this entry supports the axis-2/axis-3 separation and the internal structure of axis 2, and supplies NO evidence for or against the axis-1 separations, which are two of the three pairwise tests MECH-055 needs. (2) 'Separable under intervention' is a weaker property than 'non-degenerate in ordinary variance', and MECH-055's CONFIRMING wording asks for both. Berridge et al. explicitly note the components normally travel together. (3) Species and level: these are rodent microinjection and behavioural-affective-reaction results mapped onto a deep-network valence vector. The mapping is at the level of functional decomposition, not of implementation; nothing here licenses a claim that REE's particular 6-slot vector is the right carve-up.
mapping.source_context: Review synthesising primarily rodent work (nucleus accumbens shell and ventral pallidum microinjection of opioid, endocannabinoid and orexin agonists; taste-reactivity affective-reaction measures; amphetamine/dopamine sensitisation; 6-OHDA dopamine depletion), with supporting human pharmacological and clinical observations in addiction, depression and eating disorders.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high-but-not-primary: the wanting/liking dissociation is one of the most heavily replicated results in affective neuroscience and this review is its canonical short statement, but a review inherits rather than establishes evidence, so it is held below what a well-powered primary study would earn. Mapping fidelity 0.80 because the three-component carve-up is close to a literal restatement of MECH-055's axis-2/axis-3 content, docked because the paper cannot address axis 1 at all. Transfer risk 0.35: the transferred object is a functional decomposition rather than an anatomical homology, which travels comparatively well, but rodent microinjection to a 6-dimensional latent valence vector remains a long jump.
